clue.text: Careless friends from the east needing career

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left, so the word for friends runs backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
to career is to rush headlong, to dash

explanation.surface: Someone's friends arrive from the east, apparently in need of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun meaning a profession, but it is the verb: to rush along.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and carelessly, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Separates and suddenly shows an interest, holding power line

indicators.note: holding means the phrase for showing interest keeps the next letters inside it

parts.note: to sit up is to start paying attention

explanation.surface: Someone breaks up a fight and then perks up at a power cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who split up separate, ending their relationship.

clue.text: Skinless sausages may produce such emotion

indicators.note: skinless means the outside letters are peeled away from the word for sausages

parts.note: bangers is British slang for sausages

explanation.surface: Sausages without skins might make a diner cross.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGERS is everyday British slang for sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is the feeling one might have at skinless sausages, an emotion like rage.

clue.text: Lose heart as pride is shattered?

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone becomes downcast as their self-esteem is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, to become disheartened.

clue.text: Mock poor actor after onset of stress

indicators.note: after means the poor actor follows the first letter
onset of means the beginning, the first letter of stress

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting performer

explanation.surface: A bad actor is ridiculed once the strain begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake, and mock as an adjective means imitation or pretend.

clue.text: Answer thought to be happily occupied

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about an answer and enjoys doing so.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amused is to be entertained, pleasantly occupied by something.

clue.text: Pain — managed amazingly without New Zealand!

indicators.note: managed means handled and reworked, so the letters are rearranged
without means certain letters are left out of the pool

explanation.surface: Someone got through their pain remarkably well without going to New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Myalgia is the medical term for muscle ache.

clue.text: Propose a fresh area for such a programme

indicators.note: fresh means new, so these letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a new space for a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: a soap opera is the kind of programme the anagram suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama, a type of broadcast.

clue.text: Dredge unfinished part of swimming pool

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: the deep end is part of a swimming pool

explanation.surface: Someone digs out an incomplete section of a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge a channel is to scoop out its bed, making it lower and further down.

clue.text: Pass law delayed by members holding one

indicators.note: holding means the word for members keeps the next piece inside it

parts.note: legs are limbs, members of the body
I is the Roman numeral one
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A bill is held up by politicians who are hanging on to a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests Members of Parliament, but it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which a parliament does by passing them.

clue.text: Move to Dubai, say, covering golf?

indicators.note: covering means the word for Dubai surrounds the letter for golf

parts.note: Dubai is an example of an emirate
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone relocates to Dubai, perhaps for the golf.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to move away from one's country to settle in another.

clue.text: Conscious of a revolutionary green European

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for green is read backwards

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced

explanation.surface: Someone knows about an inexperienced radical from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aware of something means knowing about it, being mindful of it.

clue.text: Husband interrupting walk and train of thought

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the word for walk

parts.note: to tread is to walk

explanation.surface: A husband breaks in on someone's stroll and their musings.
explanation.definitionFit: One loses the thread of an argument: the connected line running through a chain of ideas.

clue.text: Identify problem of floundering dog in sea

indicators.note: floundering means thrashing about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone works out what is wrong with a dog struggling in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To diagnose is to identify an illness or fault from its symptoms.

clue.text: Know, oddly, about wild angora jumper

indicators.note: about means the odd letters go round the rearranged wool
oddly means the odd-numbered letters of know are taken
wild means unruly, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone knows strangely about an untamed angora sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for a sweater, and angora is a wool, but here it means an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo is a hopping marsupial, so it is a jumper.

clue.text: Part of car transport cost after European articles

indicators.note: after means the cost of transport is placed following the articles

parts.note: UN is a French article and DER a German one
carriage is the charge for transporting goods

explanation.surface: A buyer pays shipping for a car component after buying some European items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests goods for sale, but it means grammatical words like 'the' and 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: The undercarriage is the supporting chassis beneath a vehicle, one of its parts.

clue.text: Take apart and amend list for distribution

indicators.note: distribution means spreading out and redistributing, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone breaks down and revises a mailing list.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle something is to take it to pieces.

clue.text: City school having to cover D-day

indicators.note: having to cover means the school's name wraps round the next piece

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school
read as D plus day, with Mon the abbreviation for Monday, a day

explanation.surface: A school's city must account for the invasion anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'D-day' suggests the 1944 invasion, but it is split into D and a day (MON).
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the capital city of Alberta in Canada.

clue.text: Dexterity shown by the French in view of worker

indicators.note: in means the French article is put inside the phrase for view of

parts.note: in sight of means in view of, so sight of stands for view of
le is French for the
a hand is a worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: The French show skill when watched by a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is manual skill in conjuring tricks, a kind of nimbleness.

clue.text: Leading lady has kiss for Mike, say

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: an empress is a female ruler, a leading lady
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
X is the symbol for a kiss

explanation.surface: The star actress gets a kiss from someone called Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests a star actress, but it is a woman leading a country.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a view is to say or voice it.

clue.text: The wreckage of many buried in brief notoriety

indicators.note: buried in means the word for many is put inside
brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: fame is notoriety
lots means many

explanation.surface: Much of the wreckage is buried by fleeting notoriety.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating debris from a wrecked ship.

clue.text: Church group attached to old cat

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lot is a group, a batch

explanation.surface: A church group is attached to an old cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild feline of the Americas.

clue.text: Conservative with baskets of food and drink

parts.note: hampers are wicker baskets of picnic food

explanation.surface: A Tory turns up with picnic hampers and something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAMPERS is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is a slang word for champagne, a sparkling drink.

clue.text: Vessel returning to dock in low country

indicators.note: a ship docks in a port, so the reversed vessel goes inside the word for low

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for vessel reads backwards

parts.note: a can is a vessel, a container

explanation.surface: A ship comes back to berth in the Low Countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low country' suggests the Netherlands, but 'low' is the cow's moo; MONACO is a principality on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny sovereign state on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Fireguards put up to protect carpenter's tool

indicators.note: put up means raised, so in a down clue the letters read bottom to top
to protect means the letters are held inside the word fireguards

explanation.surface: Fireguards are installed to keep a woodworker's tool safe.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a boring tool for making holes in wood.

clue.text: Live with a socially acceptable boyfriend

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone moves in with a respectable boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer.

clue.text: 'Bubbles' mostly must be Turner

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for bubbles is used

parts.note: lather is a froth of soap bubbles

explanation.surface: A painting called Bubbles must surely be by Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbles' is a famous Millais painting and Turner a painter, but Turner here means a machine that turns wood or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins a workpiece so it can be shaped, so it is a turner.

clue.text: Express regret in public for lapse

indicators.note: in means the word for expressing regret is put inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
to sigh is to express regret or sorrow

explanation.surface: Someone apologises publicly for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made by failing to notice something, a lapse of attention.

clue.text: Person who believes he must replace women in dance

indicators.note: must replace means the word he takes the place of the letter for women

parts.note: the twist is a 1960s dance

explanation.surface: A believer says a man must take the women's place in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist believes in God, so is a believer.

clue.text: Rehearsal of Spooner's card game at an end

indicators.note: a reference to Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: rummy is a card game
done means finished, at an end

explanation.surface: A rehearsal for a card game that has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of RUMMY DONE gives DUMMY RUN, with DONE sounding like it rhymes with RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy run is a practice attempt or trial, a rehearsal.
